text_en: EMS-98 rates observed damage to buildings on five grades (G1 negligible to slight, G2 moderate, G3 substantial to heavy, G4 very heavy, G5 destruction), separately for masonry and reinforced-concrete buildings. Grades describe damage actually seen, not the expected performance or risk of the building.

EMS-98 masonry buildings, grade G1 (negligible to slight): Hair-line cracks in very few walls; only small pieces of plaster fall; loose stones fall from upper parts in very few cases. No structural damage.
EMS-98 masonry buildings, grade G2 (moderate): Cracks in many walls; fairly large pieces of plaster fall; chimneys partly collapse. Slight structural damage.

EMS-98 masonry buildings, grade G3 (substantial to heavy): Large and extensive cracks in most walls; roof tiles detach; chimneys fracture at the roof line; individual non-structural elements fail. Moderate structural damage.
EMS-98 masonry buildings, grade G4 (very heavy): Serious failure of walls; partial structural failure of roofs and floors. Heavy structural damage.
EMS-98 masonry buildings, grade G5 (destruction): Total or near-total collapse of the building. Very heavy structural damage.

EMS-98 reinforced-concrete buildings, grade G1 (negligible to slight): Fine cracks in plaster over frame members or at the base of walls; fine cracks in partitions and infill walls. No structural damage.

EMS-98 reinforced-concrete buildings, grade G2 (moderate): Cracks in columns and beams of frames and in structural walls; cracks in partitions and infill walls; brittle cladding and plaster fall; mortar falls from joints of wall panels. Slight structural damage.

EMS-98 reinforced-concrete buildings, grade G3 (substantial to heavy): Cracks in columns and beam-column joints at the base of frames; spalling of concrete cover and buckling of reinforcement bars; large cracks in partitions and infill walls; individual infill panels fail. Moderate structural damage.

EMS-98 reinforced-concrete buildings, grade G4 (very heavy): Large cracks in structural elements with compression failure of concrete and fracture of reinforcement; bond failure of beam bars; tilting of columns; collapse of a few columns or of a single upper floor. Heavy structural damage.
EMS-98 reinforced-concrete buildings, grade G5 (destruction): Collapse of the ground floor or of parts (for example wings) of the building. Very heavy structural damage.

Our assessment, not a source statement: from overhead or oblique imagery, G5 collapse and the more severe wall, roof or floor failures of G4 can be visible, G3 may show only as displaced roof tiles, broken chimneys or debris, and G1 to G2 (fine cracks, plaster fall) are generally not visible. Interior and crack-level evidence is not available remotely.

The 2025 Turkish regulation on post-disaster building damage assessment (published in the Official Gazette on 22 June 2025, no. 32934) enters into force on 22 December 2026 (amendment of 17 December 2025, no. 33110, which also renamed the 'final' damage assessment stage 'initial'). It was therefore not the rule applied to the February 2023 earthquakes.
term_tr: Afetler Sonrası Bina Hasar Tespiti Yönetmeliği: yürürlük

text_en: The regulation defines ten damage classes with codes: 0 (no damage), 2 (slight), 4 (moderate), 6 (heavy), AYB (to be demolished urgently), 8 (collapsed), DD, GB, TE and KD. Codes 0, 2, 4, 6 and 8 continue the 2014 circular's scheme; AYB, DD, GB, TE and KD are listed as codes in the 2025 text. Expansions of DD, GB, TE and KD are not recorded in this knowledge base.
term_tr: Hasar sınıfları ve kodları: 0, 2, 4, 6, AYB, 8, DD, GB, TE, KD

text_en: The assessment covers only damage caused by the latest disaster, judged from observation; it does not measure the building's seismic performance, safety margin or risk, and pre-existing deterioration or construction defects are not rated as disaster damage.
term_tr: Yalnız son afetin hasarı; performans/risk ölçülmez

text_en: External inspection, reinforced-concrete and masonry buildings: if the whole building has collapsed (overall collapse) the result is 'Yıkık' (class 8, collapsed).
External inspection: partial collapse of the building, or collapse of one or more storeys, gives 'AYB' (to be demolished urgently).
term_tr: Dıştan inceleme: kısmi veya kat göçmesi → Acil yıktırılacak (AYB)

text_en: External inspection, masonry buildings only: clearly visible out-of-plane rotation of a wall, or a wall that has collapsed, gives 'AYB'.
term_tr: Yığma: düzlem dışı belirgin duvar dönmesi veya yıkılmış duvar → AYB

text_en: External inspection: permanent horizontal displacement between storeys d greater than 0.01 of storey height h gives 'heavy damage' (class 6); d greater than 0.03 h gives 'AYB'.
term_tr: Katlar arası kalıcı yatay yer değiştirme: d>0,01h Ağır; d>0,03h AYB

text_en: External inspection: rigid rotation of the building caused by differential foundation settlement greater than 1 degree gives 'heavy damage'; greater than 3 degrees gives 'AYB'.
term_tr: Temelde farklı oturmadan rijit dönme: θ>1° Ağır; θ>3° AYB

text_en: External inspection: uniform settlement of more than one third of the storey height (h/3), or settlement that prevents use of the building, gives 'heavy damage'.
term_tr: Üniform oturma > h/3 veya kullanımı engelliyorsa → Ağır

text_en: Assessment has two steps, external then internal inspection. The external rules are applied in order (collapse, then storey or wall failure, then drift, then rotation, then settlement); the first rule that applies decides and inspection stops. If no rule applies and there is no obvious damage making entry dangerous, the assessment moves to internal inspection.
term_tr: Dıştan inceleme sırası; karar çıkmazsa içeriden inceleme

text_en: Internal inspection, reinforced concrete: element damage types O (none), A (crack up to 0.5 mm), B (crack 0.5 to 3 mm or crushed or spalled cover), C (crack above 3 mm or very slight bar buckling), D (bar rupture or buckling, core concrete crushing, permanent shortening or shear deformation). Measured with a crack gauge inside the building; not observable from imagery.

Internal inspection, masonry: element damage types A (crack up to 1 mm), B (1 to 5 mm or loss of joint mortar), C (5 to 10 mm or crushed masonry), D (above 10 mm or marked deformation or loss of structural integrity). Measured with a crack gauge; not observable from imagery.

Building category 1 (reinforced concrete up to 10 storeys and under 600 square metres of floor area; masonry up to 5 storeys) is classified by counting damaged elements: reinforced concrete into No damage, Slight, Moderate, Heavy, AYB; masonry category 1 only into No damage, Slight, Heavy. Category 2 uses a weighted damage ratio (weights A 0.20, B 0.40, C 0.70, D 1.00; above 60 percent gives AYB); category 3 needs detailed engineering inspection.
term_tr: Bina kategorileri ve hasar sınıflarının içeriden belirlenmesi

text_en: Our reading of the regulation, not a quoted rule: 'no damage', 'slight' and 'moderate' classes are assigned only after internal inspection, so they cannot be issued from imagery alone; only the external rules (collapse, storey failure, large drift, rotation, settlement) can in principle be checked remotely, and even these need a view that shows the geometry. When these rules cannot be checked the honest remote output is 'cannot be determined remotely, internal inspection required'.
Aerial vehicle imagery (EO/IR) may be used for assessment only for damage to the roof, gable wall and chimney.
term_tr: Hava aracı görüntüsü yalnız çatı, kalkan duvar, baca hasarında

text_en: The regulation includes classes for buildings that could not be entered or whose damage could not be determined (codes GB and TE), so 'not determined' is a recognised official outcome rather than a failure to report.
term_tr: GB / TE: girilemeyen / tespit edilemeyen bina sınıfları

text_en: The 2014 AFAD damage assessment circular defines assessment as observational rating of the damage a disaster caused to a building; it applies only to the latest disaster, does not reveal performance or risk, and has three stages: disaster-effect determination, final damage assessment, and objection.
term_tr: Hasar Tespit Genelgesi: kapsam ve aşamalar

text_en: Damage degrees in the 2014 circular's forms: no damage (0), slight (2), moderate (4), heavy (6), collapsed (8). Urgent demolition is handled by a separate report form, not by a degree code.
term_tr: Hasarsız 0, Az 2, Orta 4, Ağır 6, Yıkık 8; acil yıktırılacak ayrı form

text_en: Class descriptions in the 2014 circular are observational and use crack width: slight damage 1 to 4 mm; moderate about 5 to 10 mm in load-bearing walls; heavy above 10 mm, widespread shear failure or leaning from the vertical. These values come from a noisy OCR page and are not yet visually verified.
term_tr: Az 1–4 mm; orta 5–10 mm; ağır >10 mm (sayfa doğrulaması bekliyor)

text_en: If the inside of a building cannot be inspected, no rating is given, except that a building can be rated without entering when most load-bearing elements are seen from outside to be heavily damaged, collapsed, displaced or partly collapsed.
term_tr: İçi incelenemeyen bina: değerlendirme yapılmaz; dıştan belirgin ağır hasar varsa girmeden derecelendirilebilir

text_en: In the 2014 circular urgent demolition ('acil yıktırılacak') is decided with its own form (Annex 2), outside the 0/2/4/6/8 degree scale; in the 2023 reporting it appeared as a separate class.

Aydoğdu Gürbüz and Aslan (2023) state that the forms and damage degrees used in the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes come from the 14.04.2014 damage assessment circular, that assessment needs external and internal technical inspection, and that official reporting (HTS, 12 June 2023) had a separate 'could not be assessed' class of 132,780 buildings and an 'urgent demolition' class of 21,208 buildings. The article does not explain why assessment was not possible. The printed total in its Table 3 does not match the sum of rows and is not used here.
term_tr: 2023'te esas alınan düzenleme ve 'Tespit yapılamadı' sınıfı

text_en: DisasterM3 building label 'intact': no visible sign of structural damage, water intrusion, displaced roof covering or burn marks.

DisasterM3 building label 'damaged': partial structural damage such as missing roof members, visible cracks or partial collapse of a wall or roof; the label can also cover partly burned buildings and buildings surrounded by water, mud or volcanic flow.
DisasterM3 building label 'destroyed': completely collapsed, burned, partly or fully covered by water or mud, or no longer present.

DisasterM3 annotates building damage as instance masks with three classes (intact, damaged, destroyed) following FEMA guidelines; the dataset has no EMS-98 grade and no Turkish regulation class as reference labels.

Our proposed mapping, not a sourced one: dataset class 'intact' corresponds roughly to EMS-98 G0 to G1 and regulation classes 0 and 2. Grades G1 and class 2 are not visible from above, so 'intact' means 'no damage visible from imagery'. The regulation does not issue 0, 2 or 4 without internal inspection.

Our proposed mapping, not a sourced one: dataset class 'damaged' corresponds roughly to EMS-98 G2 to G4 and regulation classes 4 and 6 and part of AYB. The boundary at G4 against AYB is not one-to-one; external drift and rotation thresholds (above 0.01 h and 1 degree) point to heavy damage.
term_tr: damaged ↔ EMS-98 G2–G4 ↔ yönetmelik 4, 6, AYB'nin bir kısmı (bizim öneri)

text_en: Our proposed mapping, not a sourced one: dataset class 'destroyed' corresponds roughly to EMS-98 G5, regulation class 8 (collapsed) and AYB from partial or storey collapse. Collapse of a lower storey may not be fully visible from above.
term_tr: destroyed ↔ EMS-98 G5 ↔ yönetmelik 8, AYB (bizim öneri)

text_en: Our comparison: the 2025 regulation continues the 2014 circular (codes 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, same principles of latest-disaster-only and no performance claim). New in 2025 is a numeric external-inspection method with thresholds (0.01 h, 0.03 h, 1 degree, 3 degrees, h/3) and urgent demolition as a degree code; the 2014 circular described external inspection qualitatively. The two texts are separate sources in this knowledge base.
